submission.natural_language_explanation: L0/H2 is a retrospective context-averaging head: it attends broadly over everything read so far (near-uniform on random sequences, mildly preferring frequent tokens, no previous-token or induction structure), so its write is the running average of those tokens' OV values and its strength is how far that average lies from its scan-average write - the frequent-function-word mean (' and' 0.66, ' of' 0.67, ' by' 0.71, ' in' 0.95, whitespace 0.7-1.4), with determiners and commas at the far end (' the' 5.8, ' a' 5.4, ',' 5.0, ' an' 4.9). It is therefore active (3.4-4.9, i.e. 0.7-1.0 of max) wherever a determiner or comma dominates the tokens read so far - above all in a text's first six tokens, where a single opening determiner or comma is nearly all it has averaged (all 20 of its top scan examples sit there), and mid-text in comma- or determiner-heavy lists (3.3-4.0) - while text made only of its mean-adjacent words (' and', ' of', ' by', ' from', ' in', whitespace) stays at 0.6-1.3, below the 1.21 active line, and rare content nouns (3.0-3.4 from the mean, e.g. 'lithium', 'collisions', 'proton') lift a clause only to about 2-3.
